from.place: proof, diagonal step: a Koszul-regular immersion is perfect

title: A Koszul-regular closed immersion is perfect
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let i:Z\to Y be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that every point of Y has an affine open neighbourhood U=\operatorname{Spec}A on which the ideal I\subset A of Z\cap U is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence of A [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Then i_*\mathcal O_Z is locally quasi-isomorphic to the bounded Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] on that sequence, whose terms are finite free modules. Consequently i is a perfect closed immersion [def-sc-perfect-closed-immersion], and i_*\mathcal O_Z is a perfect complex on Y [def-pc-perfect-complex].

source.place: Tag 068C, Lemma 37.61.7 (a Koszul-regular immersion of schemes is perfect)

proof.text: For every affine chart, use the existing normalized integer-indexed Koszul quotient augmentation. Compose with extendSingleIso and take the preimage through fullyFaithfulExtendFunctor. Its extension is the original quasi-isomorphism composed with an isomorphism, so quasiIso_extendMap_iff proves that the resulting natural-number-indexed augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism.

The Koszul terms are exterior powers of Fin r →₀ A. Mathlib exteriorPower.instFree and instFinite give freeness and finiteness. The exterior-power basis has index Set.powersetCard (Fin r) n. If r<n, card_le_univ shows this index is empty; the basis representation then proves that the term is a subsingleton, hence a zero object.

Apply the affine quotient resolution sheafification theorem to the augmentation of Step 1 and each quotient presentation. Combine its quasi-isomorphism with the term properties of Step 2 to prove the full universal chart clause.

At each point choose the chart in the hypothesis. Bundle the explicit Koszul chain complex and augmentation of Step 1 into a ProjectiveResolution: free modules are projective. Its finite and projective term properties follow from Step 2, and choose r+1 as the vanishing threshold. Insert this resolution and the original quotient presentation directly into IsPerfectClosedImmersion.

On each chosen chart, apply the local strictly perfect model theorem to the sheafified augmentation of Step 3, using the finite free terms and bound of Step 2. Insert its complex and derived isomorphism into the pointwise definition of Scheme.IsPerfect.
